vulnerabilities.description: glob 10.2.0-10.4.5: Command injection vulnerability (GHSA-5j98-mcp5-4vw2). Uses shell:true allowing command injection via glob patterns. Used indirectly via @next/eslint-plugin-next.

Next.js 14.2.35: Multiple DoS and security vulnerabilities including HTTP request smuggling in rewrites (GHSA-ggv3-7p47-pfv8), Image Optimizer DoS, XSS in CSP nonces (GHSA-ffhc-5mcf-pf4q), Server Components DoS.
PostCSS <8.5.10: XSS vulnerability via unescaped </style> in CSS stringify output (GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93). Could allow CSS injection attacks.
Memory JSON file created with default permissions (mode 0o666). If containing sensitive configuration, any local user can read. Sensitive data exposed.
Temporary files created without explicit permissions. GitHub content could be read by other system users.
Session ID generated using Date.now() which is predictable. Should use crypto.randomBytes() for cryptographic security.
Session JSON files created without explicit file permissions. Session context could be readable by other local users.
Google Analytics loaded from external CDN without Subresource Integrity (SRI). Could be compromised for XSS attacks.
JSON parsing errors silently caught without logging. Corrupted memory files fail silently without alerting users.
File operations on dynamic paths without normalization. Should use path.resolve() for defense in depth.
Build artifacts in version control. Should be gitignored and regenerated at deploy time.

recommendations: CRITICAL: Update Next.js to 16.2.6+ to fix DoS vulnerabilities, XSS flaws, and HTTP request smuggling
CRITICAL: Update glob to 10.5.0+ to prevent command injection vulnerability
CRITICAL: Update PostCSS to 8.5.10+ to fix CSS-based XSS vulnerability
HIGH: Fix file permissions in helper scripts using fs.writeFileSync(path, data, { mode: 0o600 })
HIGH: Replace Date.now() session ID generation with crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex')
MEDIUM: Add Subresource Integrity (SRI) to Google Analytics external script
MEDIUM: Add error logging in memory.js JSON parsing to detect and report file corruption
MEDIUM: Run npm audit in CI/CD pipeline and fail builds on high/critical vulnerabilities
LOW: Remove /out directory from git and regenerate at build time
LOW: Normalize file paths using path.resolve() in statusline.js for defense in depth
